title: [spec-gap][R-12-107] Rate-limit keying violates MUST NOT key-on-IID: C 1-byte, Python 64-bit; spec requires 128-bit/OSCORE identity
description: spec/12-apps.md:1873 (18.10.3): confessions rate limiting MUST NOT key on an extracted IID; key is sender OSCORE identity (pairwise: sender/recipient pair; group: (group ctx, Sender ID)) or full 16-byte IPv6 source; all posts from a node MUST be charged to a single accounting entry (group exempt). Also 18.9:1740 same MUST for deaddrop. Evidence: C keys both resources on 1 byte (iid7 = peer_eui64[7], coap_dtn.c:193-205 deaddrop, :497 confessions — 256-bucket collision domain); Python keys confessions on low 64 bits (confessions.py:118, test_native_0200_source_iid_keys_rate codifies the divergence) but deaddrop correctly uses OSCORE identity (deaddrop.py:114-149); Rust confessions key is caller-supplied (confessions.rs:785); pairwise-pair and group-(ctx,SenderID) keying unimplemented everywhere. Related fixture bug: test/vectors/deaddrop.json rate_limit_rejection (:67-77) expects 5.03 for rate limiting where spec 18.9 mandates 4.29 + Retry-After; Rust test rate_limit_rejection_matches_vector (deaddrop_vectors.rs:339) pins the wrong code — vector should be corrected to 4.29, not the test weakened. Placement: coap_dtn.c keying, confessions.py:118, confessions.rs, deaddrop.json fixture + rust vector test.
